questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to experience different landscapes but stay in Scandinavia to explore my neighboring countries. 
Also NMBU was very easy to communicate with and the course catalogue was easy accesible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: KU was a little slower with communication and info wasn't as structured.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, NMBU managed everything perfectly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Welcoming week, mentor, people to reach out to

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Both student collectives and houses. I chose a house which was calmer than the collectives, but maybe not as social.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Big kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Choose the collectives at pentagon if you want a lot of people around and parties and events, but choose the house or other places for a calmer place with more norwegian people also. I

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The easiest was to call them, and then i was perfectly guided through everything. But it was also easy to figure out on their webpage. But KU wasn't aware of the registration dates so i registered too late but NMBU worked it out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Phonecalls, mails and structured webpages

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything i applied for even though one of the classes was marked as full. I just asked the course responsible by mail.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Contact the course responsibles to get more info. 
I was also surprised that i could manage 30 ects points in the "vår parallel" but that was perfectly manageable. Januar and Juni blok is just to spread out a normal semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One of my courses was a little easy, but still interesting! I was a little surprised that a cource called an "introduction course" was still built upon previous years of education because it was at the second year of the study programme.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
If you choose courses in your study field, then the level is a little easier but you can challenge yourself by taking courses outside of your field. 
Furthermore NMBU is focusing very much on making people pass the courses, and not many people fail them.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
They spread out the exam in multiple assignments in a lot of courses, which makes it easier to pass. 
The classes are smaller and you are in close contact with your teacher. 
But the style is mostly the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Landskapsforståelse 15 ects
Politisk Økologi 10 ects
Håndtegning 5 ects

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Landskapsforståese is very theoretic and elaborates on aestetichs and experiencing landscapes as an interconnected phenomenon between human and nature. This also makes it less classic project based and you are doing stories and movies about landscapes.
Politisk Økologi is a very good introduction course, with lectures of a lot of different specialists and a lot of discussion. Very good course to investigate norwegian politics and ecological challenges. It was hard for me becuase it was out of my studyfield, with dfferent theories and methods.
Håndtegning was cool and a nice different kind of course, a little too less landscape architecture relevant.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: NMBU firluftsliv is great!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many associations! hard to interegate fully with, but fun to experience and be around.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Can recommend folkdance, outdoor club and foodsharing

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel! 
Oslomarka is right around the corner, trains are so nice, go kayaking, use the libraries in Oslo, go to the Islands, go skiing, swim and sauna

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, speaking the language was very helpful

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: try norwegian, go to associations, go to parties and bars, ask a lot of questions, get out of the exchangestudent bubble

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The high costs

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nature, openminded people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use Oslo a lot, it is so close and Ås can easily get small.
Balance studies and spare time, you will pass your courses dont worry

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the gear rental, maybe choose courses in the same programme so that you follow a class and can get to know them better, walk around and travel!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature experience and to get to know a new city and culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: A broken foot

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Bring alcohol and cigarettes from home

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
